title: Should we write minus three less than minus four, or the other way?
description: The floors minus three and minus four are placed on the line to find which sign goes between them. The lower floor is the smaller number. Keeko thinks minus four is greater because four is greater than three, and floor minus four lying below breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: below the ground, the lower floor is the smaller number. Watch for students who compare only the digits and say minus four is greater.

video_script.why: A child learns that the lower floor is the smaller number, even for floors below the ground.
video_script.substitution: the book's own floors minus three and minus four on the floor line
video_script.anchor: the floors minus three and minus four on the floor line of Ruhee
video_script.wrong_answer: minus four is greater than minus three
video_script.wrong_move: compares the digits four and three and ignores that floor minus four lies further down
video_script.payoff_line: The lower floor is the smaller number, even below the ground.

final_answer.value: −4 < −3 (Floor −4 is lower than Floor −3). It is also correct to write −3 > −4.
final_answer.spoken: floor minus four is lower than floor minus three, so minus four is less than minus three

names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: the sign before the floors are compared
maths_rules: Floor +3 is lower than Floor +4, so +3 < +4 and +4 > +3.
−3 is three floors down and −4 is four floors down.
Floor −4 is lower than floor −3, so −4 < −3 and −3 > −4.
video_script.design: One idea: the lower floor is the smaller number. One floor line throughout. Keeko's doubt is broken by floor minus four lying below floor minus three.
